news.headline: Commerce Dept Closes Nvidia Chip Export Loophole; NVDA Dips on China Risk
news.body: The U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security issued guidance on May 31 mandating that advanced AI processors—including Nvidia's Blackwell and Rubin chips and AMD's MI350x—now require export licenses when sold to Chinese-headquartered entities regardless of where delivery occurs, closing a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to route purchases through Southeast Asian subsidiaries. The rule change erases a workaround Chinese companies had exploited for roughly a year via Malaysian and Singaporean subsidiaries. Nvidia shares, which had surged on the RTX Spark PC chip launch, reversed intraday to trade down ~1.5% as the export crackdown could block hundreds of thousands of chips from reaching Chinese end-users. The ruling adds a new regulatory overhang to Nvidia's data-center revenue outlook and raised fresh concerns about AMD's international sales pipeline.

news.headline: Nvidia Unveils RTX Spark PC Superchip at Computex; NVDA +6%, Dell +10%, HP +8%
news.body: At Computex 2026 in Taipei, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang unveiled the RTX Spark superchip—an Arm-based processor co-developed with Microsoft and MediaTek combining a Blackwell GPU with a custom Grace CPU and 128GB unified memory—marking Nvidia's entry into the PC market. The chip will debut in fall 2026 Windows laptops and desktops from Dell, HP, Microsoft, Lenovo, ASUS, and MSI, directly challenging Qualcomm's Snapdragon X franchise; Qualcomm fell ~7% on competitive fears while Intel dropped ~6%. Nvidia shares surged more than 6% intraday to near $222, and Dell Technologies and HP Inc gained 10% and 8% respectively as investors priced in new PC upgrade supercycle potential. Huang also confirmed Nvidia's Vera Rubin data-center CPUs are in full production, with early customers including Anthropic, OpenAI, and CoreWeave.

news.headline: IBM Surges 12%+ as Trump Praise Video Goes Viral and Barclays Initiates at Overweight
news.body: IBM stock surged up to 15% in premarket and closed ~12% higher on June 1 after a December 2025 White House roundtable video resurfaced on social media showing President Trump calling CEO Arvind Krishna 'a legend' and predicting the stock would rise further, accumulating over 700,000 views. The social-media-driven rally was compounded by Barclays initiating coverage with an Overweight rating and a $350 price target, citing IBM's highly stable enterprise software customer base and nearly 50% software revenue mix. Wedbush also reaffirmed an Outperform rating at $320, calling IBM the center of a '$1 trillion value creation engine.' The move extends IBM's largest weekly percentage gain since April 2001, itself driven by a U.S.-backed quantum computing foundry announcement the prior week.

news.headline: Berkshire Hathaway Acquires Taylor Morrison for $8.5B; TMHC Pops 22%
news.body: Berkshire Hathaway agreed to acquire homebuilder Taylor Morrison Home Corporation for $72.50 per share in cash—a 24% premium to its May 29 close—valuing the equity at ~$6.8 billion and total enterprise value at ~$8.5 billion. The deal is the first major strategic acquisition under new CEO Greg Abel, who succeeded Warren Buffett at the start of 2026, and would create the fourth-largest homebuilder in the U.S. by combining Taylor Morrison with Berkshire's existing Clayton Homes and building products businesses. Taylor Morrison shares surged 22% on June 1 and shares of peer homebuilders broadly gained as investors interpreted the move as a long-term vote of confidence in the U.S. housing recovery. The all-cash deal is expected to close in the second half of 2026 pending regulatory and shareholder approval.

news.headline: Software Stocks Stage Broad Rally as Huang Dismisses AI Disruption Fears
news.body: Enterprise software stocks extended a two-day surge on June 1 after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang declared at Computex that agentic AI would expand—not destroy—demand for software, arguing that AI agents will use 'more tools than ever.' ServiceNow surged ~10%, Atlassian gained ~15%, Salesforce rose ~8.5%, and Adobe and Workday each advanced ~5%, with the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV) gaining ~4.7% on the day. The rally reversed months of sector underperformance driven by fears that AI agents would cannibalize traditional enterprise software, and IBM's parallel 12% gain added further momentum. Markets now price software platforms as essential AI infrastructure rather than disruption victims, a significant re-rating with broad implications for enterprise tech valuations.

news.headline: Nikkei and KOSPI retreat as Trump signals indifference to Iran peace talks collapsing
news.body: Asia-Pacific markets sold off on June 2 after U.S. President Trump told CNBC he was indifferent to Iran peace negotiations failing, saying 'I don't care if they're over, honestly.' Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 1.32% and the Topix declined 1.14%, unwinding part of the prior session's SoftBank-led gains. South Korea's KOSPI fell 1.92% and the small-cap Kosdaq dropped 3.13% as profit-taking set in after its record-setting run. Brent crude remained elevated near $96/barrel, with ongoing Strait of Hormuz disruptions sustaining an oil-price risk premium that compresses margins for energy-intensive Japanese and Korean manufacturers.

news.headline: TSMC Hits $2.28T Market Cap as Computex AI Announcements Drive 5% Surge
news.body: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co surged more than 5% on June 1, pushing its market capitalisation above $2.28 trillion to a record high, as Nvidia's unveiling of its Vera Rubin AI computing platform at GTC Taipei — to be manufactured entirely on TSMC's 3nm process — cemented TSMC's role as the indispensable backbone of global AI infrastructure. A separate catalyst emerged from supply-chain sources indicating TSMC plans to raise 3nm wafer pricing by up to 15% in H2 2026, with fully utilised capacity already generating extended customer wait times. Taiwan's TAIEX benchmark crossed the 45,000 level for the first time, with TSMC, Foxconn, MediaTek, and Quanta all simultaneously hitting all-time highs. TSMC's US ADRs climbed ~5.4% to $441, sharply outperforming a flat S&P 500, as investors priced in a structurally higher revenue and margin outlook heading into the June 4 shareholder meeting.

news.headline: Samsung Electronics hits all-time high, KOSPI record as HBM4E chips ship and strike averted
news.body: Samsung Electronics surged over 10% on June 1 to close at a record high of 347,500 KRW, becoming the first Korean stock to breach 2,000 trillion won in market cap. Three simultaneous catalysts drove the move: the company began shipping HBM4E memory samples to customers globally ahead of rivals, a union strike threat involving ~48,000 workers was averted after 74% of members approved a new pay deal, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was expected to visit Seoul this week for meetings with Samsung and other Korean tech leaders. Goldman Sachs raised its Samsung price target to 480,000 KRW on the day, reframing memory as predictable 'AI infrastructure' rather than a cyclical commodity. The KOSPI surged 3.68%–4.31% intraday to successive record highs above 8,800, triggering an 11th sidecar circuit-breaker on program buy orders.

news.headline: Hang Seng Rises 0.7% to 25,182 as Lenovo's Record AI Earnings Lift Tech Sector
news.body: The Hang Seng Index recovered on June 1 to close up 0.7% at 25,182, as improved risk sentiment followed a tentative 60-day US-Iran ceasefire extension, with Lenovo (HKSE: 992) among the standout movers after its record FY2026 earnings print drove a near-20% share price gain the prior Friday. Lenovo reported full-year revenue of $83.1 billion — the strongest in the company's history — with AI-related sales surging 105% year-on-year to account for 33% of group revenue, while Q4 net income grew nearly six-fold to $521 million. The broader Hong Kong tech complex benefited, with Tencent Holdings gaining 2.4%, Lenovo jumping ~22% on the week, and Xiaomi adding 2.1%, as regulatory normalisation in Beijing continued to provide sector clarity. CEO Yuanqing Yang set a $100 billion revenue target within two years, anchoring the AI growth thesis that has helped the Hang Seng deliver approximately 28.7% year-to-date returns as of late May.

news.headline: SoftBank overtakes Toyota as Japan's most valuable firm after €75B France AI commitment
news.body: SoftBank Group announced plans to invest up to €75 billion ($87 billion) to build 5 GW of AI data center capacity in France, with the first phase comprising €45 billion for 3.1 GW in northern France by 2031. The announcement, made at President Macron's Choose France summit, is SoftBank's largest AI infrastructure investment in Europe and includes a partnership with Schneider Electric in Dunkirk. Shares surged 14% on June 1, extending SoftBank's year-to-date gain to over 70%, lifting it past Toyota to become Japan's most valuable company. SoftBank's $30 billion-plus stake in OpenAI generated $45 billion in gains in the fiscal year ended March, reinforcing its positioning at the core of the global AI value chain.

news.headline: WTI Surges 6–8% as Iran Halts US Talks, Threatens Hormuz Closure
news.body: WTI crude futures spiked more than 8% intraday on June 1 after Iranian media reported Tehran suspended communications with Washington in response to Israeli strikes in Lebanon and signaled preparations to fully close the Strait of Hormuz. Prices settled up ~6% above $92/barrel after Trump said Israel and Hezbollah had agreed to a halt in Lebanon and that Iran talks were continuing, pulling oil from session highs. Brent rose ~5% to above $95/barrel on the same session, with markets remaining on edge given unresolved clashes between US and Iranian forces near the strait. The move adds to a ~30% rally in crude since the Middle East conflict began in late February, with the Strait of Hormuz remaining effectively closed to normal traffic.

news.headline: Gold Holds Above $4,500 as Iran Ceasefire Talks Stall; Rate Hike Risk Caps Gains
news.body: Gold steadied above $4,500/oz on June 1–2 following a volatile week, as US-Iran ceasefire negotiations showed little progress and Washington and Tehran continued exchanging draft proposals. The metal faces a dual headwind: Middle East-driven oil inflation is fueling rate hike speculation, with markets now pricing roughly a 50% probability of at least one Fed rate hike by year-end. Silver tracked gold, steadying above $75/oz after a monthly gain of ~4%, though UBS recently cut its silver supply-deficit forecast sharply to 60–70 million oz from 300 million oz. Market focus shifts to Friday's US nonfarm payrolls and the June 16–17 Fed meeting under new Chair Kevin Warsh for the next directional catalyst.

news.headline: Copper Hits Two-Week High as Chile Posts Weakest April Output in 23 Years
news.body: Copper futures climbed above $6.40/lb on June 1, their highest in over two weeks, after Chile reported its weakest April copper production in 23 years, reinforcing tight global supply concerns. Newly appointed Codelco chairman signaled a pivot to profitability over volume maximization, raising doubts about near-term Chilean output recovery. Separately, aluminum hit its highest level since March 2022, trading at $3,730/t on June 1, up ~51% year-on-year, driven by GCC supply chain improvements for refining inputs and structural demand from AI data centers and energy transition infrastructure. Both metals are receiving additional support from the Strait of Hormuz closure disrupting sulfur and sulfuric acid supply chains critical to copper refining.

news.headline: Russia Bans Jet Fuel Exports Through November After Record Ukraine Drone Strikes
news.body: Russia announced a ban on jet fuel exports effective June 1 through November 30, 2026, after Ukrainian drone strikes set a monthly record in May, pushing Russia's crude processing rate to a 16-year low. The Yaroslavl refinery — a 300,000 bpd Gazprom Neft facility — was hit for the fourth time in a single month, with key hubs at Ryazan, Kirishi, and NORSI also damaged, collectively knocking out an estimated 25% of Russian refining capacity. The jet fuel ban follows an existing gasoline export ban in place since April, as Moscow seeks to prevent domestic shortages heading into peak summer demand. International market impact is limited given Russia exports only ~28,000–30,000 bpd of jet fuel, but the development signals worsening structural damage to Russian energy infrastructure.

news.headline: BHP Port Hedland Strike Vote Threatens World's Largest Iron Ore Export Terminal
news.body: The Electrical Trades Union formally applied to Australia's Fair Work Commission in late May 2026 to authorise a protected industrial action ballot at BHP's Port Hedland bulk export terminal — the world's largest iron ore export facility by throughput. The ~200 ETU electrical workers hold critical roles in port control systems; a successful ballot could trigger rolling stoppages, overtime bans, or full 24-hour shutdowns as early as June 30. Port Hedland is the primary gateway for BHP's Pilbara iron ore network supplying Chinese steel mills, making any disruption a systemic risk to global seaborne iron ore supply and freight markets. The threat compounds existing iron ore price pressure from elevated port stockpiles in China, weakest April Chinese steel output since 2018, and a 2.8% year-on-year decline in Chinese steel production.
